strong_findings: Frequency layer has 47 target terms/phrases and 141 collected query-source series with non-zero values from 1500 onward.
Collocation layer recovered 89 phrases with explicit semantic buckets and 10 discovered follow-up terms.
Attention layer recovered 11 Wikipedia pageview series and 14,621,041 total yearly-aggregated views in the current window.
Timeline index now has 19 anchors with clear confidence tags and category labels, including legal-rights, data/governance, and digital surveillance branches.
open_questions: Which direct, source-grade attestations for `privacy` (not dictionary-derived extracts) can be recovered with high-confidence dating?
Should legal-rights anchors and lexical-evolution anchors be separated into different downstream timeline tracks?
Which low-confidence collocation signals should be pruned versus carried for future expansion (especially AI/advertising/biometrics families)?
recommended_next_steps: Keep the modular layer outputs and re-run etymology/source-date validation with higher-confidence lexical repositories where available.
Use the 2026-frequency and collocation layers as a controlled candidate pool; do not yet lock in final semantic narratives.
Pilot a second attention source in a reproducible environment (if access policy changes) and keep it additive to Wikimedia series.
